content.title: Turning raw data into a decision
content.intro: A data analyst answers a real question by moving from raw, messy data to a clear, trustworthy conclusion.

sections.title: Start with a clear question
body: Good analysis begins before you open a spreadsheet. Decide

body.strong: what decision the answer needs to support

body: , such as whether signups dropped after a pricing change, not just "look at the data".

sections.title: Clean before you conclude
sections.body: Raw data usually has duplicates, missing values, and inconsistent formats. Cleaning it first means the patterns you find later are real, not artifacts of messy data.

diagram.title: From raw data to a decision
diagram.body: Each stage removes noise and adds meaning, until the result is something a person can act on.
diagram.label: Raw data becomes cleaned data, then analysis, then an insight, then a decision

next.title: Check the analysis foundations
next.body: Choose the clearer question and the sounder next step in two short situations.

content.title: Check data analysis foundations
content.intro: Use the question, the data, and the decision behind each choice.

questions.prompt: Which is the clearest question to start an analysis with?
options: Did signups drop after the March 1 pricing change, and by how much?
questions.explanation: A useful question names the event, the metric it affects, and asks for a measurable answer.

questions.prompt: A spreadsheet of signups has duplicate rows and blank dates. What should the analyst do first?
options: Build the chart anyway, duplicates rarely matter
Clean the duplicates and missing values before analyzing
Delete the whole dataset and ask for a new one
Ignore the dates and use only the totals
questions.explanation: Cleaning the data first keeps later patterns and conclusions trustworthy.

completion.title: You understand data analysis!
completion.body: You learned how a clear question, clean data, and honest evidence lead to a decision worth trusting.
